decisions.diagnosis: Southbound sensor produced spurious detections, mostly overnight, while northbound stayed normal; the inflated counts cannot be separated from real riding.
decisions.evidence: 00:00-05:59 southbound counts of 16, 39, 10, 18, 18 on Jun 2/4/5/6/8 (9, 5, 7, 4, 5, 9 bikes per hour through the night on Sun Jun 4), against no more than 7 on any other day of the site's 4.5-year record; daily totals of 81, 52, 53, 46 against about 15-20 before and after; weekly 247 and 273 against 110-130; northbound 254 unchanged at 19-29 per day.

series.name: Northbound (away from city)
series.evidence: Counter 212 replaced 186 at the same site after a two-week gap (186 ends 2021-11-30, 212 starts 2021-12-15), and both are RidePod 5920 piezo units. Levels match across the change: Nov 2021 13/day, Dec 2021 14/day and Jan 2022 22/day. Both counters show the same afternoon-peaked hourly profile, and in both this direction is busier than southbound.

series.name: Southbound (citybound)
series.evidence: Same like-for-like replacement. Levels match: Nov 2021 12/day, Dec 2021 14/day and Jan 2022 14/day. Both counters show the same distinctive 04:00 bump (0.9 per hour in each) and a flatter daytime profile.

summary: Site 181 was counted by two identical RidePod piezo counters in turn, 186 (2019-03 to 2021-11) and then 212 (2021-12 to 2023-07). They read comparably, so each direction is one series. The automatic zero_outage fix correctly removes a dead period from 2019-04-28 to 2019-09-30. The only fault left is a burst of spurious, largely overnight southbound counts from 2023-06-02 to 06-10, which is set to missing.
